sections.subtitle: Basic Prepositions & Their Uses
sections.content: A (to/at): direction, time, indirect object. 'Voy a Madrid' (I'm going to Madrid), 'A las tres' (At three o'clock). DE (of/from): possession, origin, material. 'El libro de Juan' (Juan's book), 'Soy de España' (I'm from Spain), 'Una mesa de madera' (A wooden table). EN (in/on/at): location, means. 'Estoy en casa' (I'm at home), 'En autobús' (By bus). CON (with): accompaniment. 'Café con leche' (Coffee with milk). POR (for/by/through): reason, means, duration, movement through. PARA (for/to): purpose, destination, deadline. SIN (without): 'Sin azúcar' (Without sugar). SOBRE (on/about): position, topic. 'Sobre la mesa' (On the table), 'Un libro sobre historia' (A book about history).

sections.subtitle: Contractions & Personal A
sections.content: CONTRACTIONS: Only two in Spanish: A + EL = AL: 'Voy al cine' (I'm going to the cinema). DE + EL = DEL: 'El libro del profesor' (The teacher's book). Never contract with other articles: a la, de la, a los, de los, etc. PERSONAL A: Use 'a' before direct objects that are people or pets. 'Veo a María' (I see María - person). 'Veo la casa' (I see the house - thing, no 'a'). 'Quiero a mi perro' (I love my dog - pet gets 'a'). Also with 'alguien' (someone), 'nadie' (no one), 'quién' (who as object): '¿A quién buscas?' (Who are you looking for?). Exception: tener doesn't use personal a: 'Tengo un hermano' (not 'a un hermano').

sections.subtitle: Prepositions of Place & Time
sections.content: PLACE: en (in/at/on - general location), a (to - direction), de (from - origin), sobre/encima de (on top of), debajo de (under), delante de (in front of), detrás de (behind), al lado de (next to), cerca de (near), lejos de (far from), entre (between/among), dentro de (inside), fuera de (outside). Examples: 'El libro está en la mesa' (on the table), 'Voy a la tienda' (to the store), 'Vengo de casa' (from home). TIME: a (at specific time), en (in month/year/season), por (during general time), de...a (from...to), desde (since/from), hasta (until), antes de (before), después de (after), durante (during specific). Examples: 'A las dos' (at two), 'En enero' (in January), 'Desde 2020' (since 2020), 'Hasta mañana' (until tomorrow).

sections.subtitle: Por vs Para: The Essential Distinction
sections.content: POR (reason/cause/exchange/movement through/duration): (1) REASON: 'Lo hago por ti' (I do it for you/because of you). (2) EXCHANGE: 'Pagué 10 euros por el libro' (I paid 10 euros for the book). (3) THROUGH/ALONG: 'Camino por la calle' (I walk through/along the street). (4) MEANS: 'Por avión' (by plane). (5) DURATION (vague): 'Estudié por dos horas' (for two hours). (6) 'Thanks for': 'Gracias por tu ayuda' (Thanks for your help). PARA (purpose/destination/deadline/recipient): (1) PURPOSE: 'Estudio para aprender' (I study to learn). (2) DESTINATION: 'Voy para Madrid' (I'm heading to/toward Madrid). (3) DEADLINE: 'Es para mañana' (It's for/due tomorrow). (4) RECIPIENT: 'Un regalo para ti' (A gift for you). (5) OPINION: 'Para mí, es fácil' (For me/In my opinion, it's easy).

sections.subtitle: Por vs Para: More Examples & Key Phrases
sections.content: COMMON EXPRESSIONS WITH POR: por favor (please), por ejemplo (for example), por fin (finally), por supuesto (of course), por lo menos (at least), por primera vez (for the first time), por si acaso (just in case), estar por (to be in favor of/about to). COMMON EXPRESSIONS WITH PARA: para siempre (forever), para nada (not at all), para que (so that - with subjunctive), estar listo para (ready for/to). TRICKY COMPARISONS: 'Trabajo por mi padre' (I work FOR my father - in his place/because of him) vs 'Trabajo para mi padre' (I work FOR my father - he's my boss/employer). 'Salgo por la puerta' (I exit THROUGH the door) vs 'Salgo para la puerta' (I'm heading TOWARD the door). Remember: POR looks backward (reason/cause), PARA looks forward (goal/purpose).

sections.subtitle: Prepositional Verbs & Complex Prepositions
sections.content: PREPOSITIONAL VERBS: Many verbs require specific prepositions. pensar EN (think about): 'Pienso en ti' (I think about you). soñar CON (dream about): 'Sueño con viajar' (I dream of traveling). depender DE (depend on): 'Depende de ti' (It depends on you). consistir EN (consist of): 'Consiste en esto' (It consists of this). casarse CON (marry): 'Se casó con María'. enamorarse DE (fall in love with): 'Me enamoré de ella'. Others: insistir en, tratar de, dejar de, empezar a, aprender a. COMPLEX PREPOSITIONS: a través de (through/across), en vez de (instead of), además de (besides), a pesar de (despite), en lugar de (instead of), acerca de (about), con respecto a (with respect to), junto a (next to), frente a (in front of/facing).

questions.question: What are the two contractions in Spanish?
questions.hint: Only a + el = al, and de + el = del contract in Spanish.

questions.question: 'Voy a el cine' or 'Voy al cine' - which is correct?
questions.hint: A + el must contract to 'al'. Voy al cine (to the cinema).

questions.question: 'El libro de el profesor' or 'El libro del profesor' - which is correct?

answers.text: El libro del profesor (de + el = del)
El libro de el profesor (no contraction)

questions.hint: De + el must contract to 'del'. El libro del profesor (the teacher's book).

questions.question: When do you use personal 'a'?

answers.text: Before direct objects that are people or pets

questions.hint: Personal a: Veo a María (person) but Veo la casa (thing, no 'a').

questions.question: 'Veo a María' vs 'Veo la casa' - Why the difference?

answers.text: María is a person (needs personal a); casa is a thing (no a)
María is feminine, casa is not
La casa needs 'la' so no room for 'a'

questions.hint: Use personal 'a' before people/pets as direct objects, not things.

questions.question: 'Tengo un hermano' or 'Tengo a un hermano' - which is correct?

answers.text: Tengo un hermano (tener doesn't use personal a)
Tengo a un hermano (needs personal a)

questions.hint: Exception: tener (to have) doesn't use personal 'a' even with people.

questions.question: What preposition indicates specific time?
questions.hint: Use 'a' for specific clock times: a las tres, a la una.

questions.question: 'En enero' means...
questions.hint: Use 'en' for months, years, and seasons: en enero, en 2020, en verano.

questions.question: 'Desde 2020' means...
questions.hint: Desde = since/from (starting point). Often paired with hasta (until).

questions.question: 'Hasta mañana' means...
questions.hint: Hasta = until (endpoint). Common farewell: ¡Hasta mañana!

questions.question: 'Lo hago por ti' - What does 'por' mean here?
questions.hint: Por = for (reason/cause). I do it BECAUSE OF you/for your sake.

questions.question: 'Estudio para aprender' - What does 'para' mean here?
questions.hint: Para = for (purpose/goal). I study IN ORDER TO learn.

questions.question: 'Pagué 10 euros por el libro' - Why 'por' not 'para'?

answers.text: Para = for prices in future only

questions.hint: Por = in exchange for. Use with prices, trades, exchanges.

questions.question: 'Un regalo para ti' - Why 'para' not 'por'?

answers.text: Por = only for things, not people

questions.hint: Para = for (recipient/destination). The gift is intended FOR you.

questions.question: 'Es para mañana' means...
questions.hint: Para = for (deadline). Homework is DUE tomorrow.

questions.question: 'Camino por la calle' means...
questions.hint: Por = through/along (movement through area). Walk THROUGH/ALONG the street.

questions.question: 'Voy para Madrid' means...
questions.hint: Para = toward/for (destination/direction). Heading IN THE DIRECTION OF Madrid.

questions.question: 'Gracias por tu ayuda' - Why 'por' not 'para'?
questions.hint: Fixed expression: Gracias POR (thanks for). Por shows the reason for gratitude.

questions.question: What does 'por favor' mean?
questions.hint: Fixed expression with por: por favor (please).

questions.question: What does 'para siempre' mean?
questions.hint: Fixed expression with para: para siempre (forever/for always).

questions.question: 'Pienso en ti' - What preposition follows 'pensar' to mean 'think about'?
questions.hint: Prepositional verb: pensar EN (think about). I think ABOUT you.

questions.question: 'Sueño con viajar' - What preposition follows 'soñar' to mean 'dream about'?
questions.hint: Prepositional verb: soñar CON (dream about/of). I dream OF traveling.

questions.question: 'Depende de ti' - What preposition follows 'depender'?
questions.hint: Prepositional verb: depender DE (depend on). It depends ON you.

questions.question: What does 'a pesar de' mean?
questions.hint: Complex preposition: a pesar de (despite). A pesar de la lluvia (despite the rain).
